newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end lower.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended slightly lower across the board on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Thursday.

"Treasury bill yields ended slightly higher today but bond prices ended lower across the board. The interbank rate eased slightly and kept most people away. Volume was only moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.90/1.85 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 1.85/1.80 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.12/2.07 percent against 2.00/1.95 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.35/98.40 from Wednesday's close of S$98.43/98.48, September 2001 at S$97.05/97.10 versus S$97.15/97.20 and June 2003 at S$95.05/95.10 against S$95.15/95.20.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to three 2-7/8 percent from Wednesday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
